section: Perspectives in Education · Ch — Teaching Methods
subject: Perspectives in Education
stem: In a cooperative-learning technique, a class of 25 is split into 5 'home groups' of 5; each member of a home group is assigned a different sub-topic and joins an 'expert group' with same-sub-topic members from other home groups to master it, then returns to teach it to their own home group — so the full topic is learned only when all members share their piece. This technique is called:
explanation: The Jigsaw Method (Elliot Aronson) creates positive interdependence — each student holds a unique 'piece of the puzzle' that the whole group needs, ensuring every member must actively contribute and teach others, unlike simpler pair-sharing techniques.

section: Perspectives in Education · Ch — Teaching Methods
subject: Perspectives in Education
stem: After posing a question, the teacher gives students a moment to reflect on their own, then has them discuss their thoughts with a neighbour, before finally inviting a few pairs to share their answer with the whole class. This simple, low-preparation cooperative technique is called:
explanation: Think-Pair-Share ensures every student first forms an individual answer (Think), tests it with a partner (Pair), and only then risks it publicly (Share) — increasing participation of shy learners compared to immediately asking for whole-class volunteers.
